name: Dutch Blue
lede: Dutch Blue is a soft grey-blue, a name that has meant different things to dictionaries and to pigment makers.

sections.title: A blue-grey and a mixture
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines Dutch blue simply as a blue-grey [1]. Garfield counts it among 221 color names drawn from peoples, along with [[tyrian-purple]] [2]. In pigment lists the term is a trade name: the Pigment Compendium notes that Fishwick (recipes of 1795-1816) gives formulations for Dutch blue that mix lead white, Paris white (fine chalk) and [[prussian-blue]] [3].

Cutting Prussian blue with white would give a pale, greyed blue, so the recipe and the dictionary's blue-grey may describe similar colors, but the books do not say so [1][3]. The swatch sits close to [[delft-blue]] in the data.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: #8D99AB is a light, low-chroma blue [9]. The books give no firm date or inventor for the name [1][3]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
